author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Indian rupee recovered from a session low Wednesday after traders said the Reserve Bank of India likely entered the currency market to slow a decline driven by higher oil prices and dollar outflows.

Reuters reported that the rupee fell to 95.2250 per U.S. dollar before recovering to 95.07 following the suspected intervention. The central bank did not confirm the action in the initial account, so the explanation remains based on traders’ assessment of market activity.

India is a major oil importer, making its currency particularly sensitive when crude prices rise because importers need more dollars to pay energy bills. Portfolio outflows can add to that demand and increase depreciation pressure.

The quoted exchange rates were intraday snapshots from September 9, not live prices, and may have changed after publication. The move shows the challenge facing the RBI: intervention can reduce abrupt volatility, but sustained oil costs and capital flows can continue to influence the currency. Later official data may clarify the scale of any central-bank operation.
dek: Traders said the Reserve Bank of India likely intervened after rising oil costs and dollar outflows pushed the currency to a session low.
headline: Indian rupee recovers after reported central-bank support
